abstract: Accurate identification of catalytic residues is central to understanding enzyme mechanisms and engineering biocatalysts, yet annotation remains challenging because experimentally validated sites are sparse. Here, we present SCOPE, a graph learning framework for catalytic residue prediction that integrates evolutionary, physicochemical, and three-dimensional structural information at the residue level. SCOPE represents enzymes as residue-level structural graphs and incorporates a Gaussian auxiliary training objective that aggregates structure-aware representations along sequence order. Evaluations across five benchmark datasets, CATH family-disjoint retraining and the external CataloDB benchmark assess predictive performance and generalization. Structural analyses associate complete catalytic-residue recovery with compact active-site arrangements. We further validated SCOPE prospectively across four enzymes using site-directed mutagenesis and activity assays, confirming multiple predicted residues as functionally important. These results support SCOPE as a framework for catalytic residue annotation and prioritizing functional sites for experimental investigation.
